answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before transacting. Like yarrow spreading only where its roots take hold, trust grows from committed capital, not a claimed name. An identity with no stake sits below the ridge of minimum trust and cannot take high-value work until it posts collateral. Peers audit behavior, and proven fraud triggers slashing: the stake is burned. A falcon-eyed verifier checks claims against the ledger, so an attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and risk losing them all.
